one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05. Broadcom reports Q4 FY26 after the close on Wednesday 2026-12-09 [5], outside the window, so there is no company print. In-window: Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 results in late October bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides; every 2026 guide was raised this year [14], so the skew is mildly positive for AI semis but widely expected. Google commentary matters for TPU sourcing ('some diversity of sources' [6]). Financing headlines (XPV tranches, Anthropic) can cut either way; the verified exposure is a $29B max backstop and a $42B undrawn note facility [3]. Short-horizon regularity: AVGO rose from a $343.64 close on Oct 1 to $377.32 today (+9.8%) [15] with no Broadcom filing; sharp, news-light runs partly reverse about as often as they extend. I take no directional view beyond a very small reversal tilt (-0.4% drift): lognormal centred on $377.32 with 13.4% monthly sigma (47%/3.5), giving P(>=377.32) = 0.488.

fair_value.method: 70% P/E on FY28 (NTM at the horizon) EPS $23.94 x 18x = $431.0, plus 30% DCF at 10.8% on FY28 FCF/share $19.87 fading 15/8/5/4% with 3% terminal = $310.3. Blend 0.7 x 431.0 + 0.3 x 310.3 = $394.8. FY28 EPS rests on AI revenue of $175B (vs management's $230B line of sight) and a 62% operating margin.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 EPS $23.94 = (revenue $231B [AI 175 + non-AI 19 + software 37] x 62% - $2.4B net interest) x 0.84 / 4.94B shares; x 18x = $431.0

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 FY26 call: 'In 2027, we have secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion.'

Management has 'line of sight' to $230B [5]. I haircut it to $175B (+52% y/y, not +100%). (a) Google dual-sourcing: Q2 call 'We fully expect that there will be some diversity of sources for them' [6]; Macquarie models AVGO's Google TPU share at ~95%/80%/65% for 2026/27/28 (sell-side estimate, not a fact) [7]. (b) House capex base: 2028 ex-China customer AI capex $2,255B vs $1,841B in 2027, +22% [14]. FY27 $115B is 6.2% of 2027 capex (115/1841); $175B is 7.8% of 2028 (175/2255), still a 1.6pt share gain, carried by the Anthropic (+10 GW in 2028) and OpenAI (>5 GW in 2028) line of sight [5]. (c) Cross-check with 10-Q purchase commitments [4]: $52,674M due FY27 against FY27 revenue of ~$167B (115 + 4.3x4 + 8.7x4) is a ratio of 0.315; $72,952M due FY28 / 0.315 = ~$231B total FY28 revenue, i.e. ~$175B AI after ~$56B non-AI. Estimate.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$4.3B [5] x 4 = $17.2B, +~5%/yr for two years = $19.0B.

Q4 FY26 guide ~$8.7B ('stabilize') [5] x 4 = $34.8B, +~3%/yr for two years = $36.9B. Q3 was $8,752M [1]; slow growth reflects VMware licensing pushback (CISPE complaint to the European Commission) [10].

Q3 FY26 non-GAAP op margin 67.9% ($20,095M / $29,591M) and gross margin 75.0% ($22,191M / $29,591M) [1]; Q4 guide GM ~73% and op margin ~66% [5]; Q2 GM 77.1% [6]. GM fell ~0.34pt per 1pt of AI revenue share (75.0% at 56.4% AI share in Q3 -> 73% at 62.4% in Q4: 16.7/29.6 and 21.7/34.8 [1][5]). At a 75.8% AI share in FY28 (175/231) that extrapolates to ~68.5% GM; opex ~5.5% of revenue (Q3 non-GAAP opex $2,096M = 7.1% [1], growing slower than revenue) gives ~63%. I take 1pt off for rack-level/memory pass-through mix (the 10-Q backstop is tied to 'AI racks' [3]): 62%. Estimate.
Q3 non-GAAP interest expense $703M [1]; implied other income ~+$98M (non-GAAP net income $16,372M / 0.84 = $19,490M pre-tax vs $20,095M - $703M = $19,392M) [1]. (703 - 98) x 4 = $2.42B.
Guided for Q4 and FY2026 'due to the impact of the global minimum tax' [5]; held for FY28 (judgment).
Q4 FY26 non-GAAP diluted share count guide ~4.94B [5] (Q3: 4,937M [1]); held flat.

(231 x 0.62 - 2.4) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $23.94. Sanity check: the same build at $230B AI gives $29.7, matching management's 'on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028' [5]. +23% vs FY27 consensus $19.39 [11].

Peer median 23.7x on next-fiscal-year EPS (11 peers, range 15.3x-60.9x) [12]; AVGO today 19.46x (377.32 / 19.39 [11]). 18x is inside the range, -24% vs the median; reasons in comps_summary (horizon EPS growth +23% vs a ~50% peer median 'EPS next Y', concentration, contingent financing exposure, margin dilution).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF/share $19.87 (0.83 x $23.94); growth 15/8/5% then 4% to FY37; terminal 3%; discount 10.8% (10y 5.31% + 5.5pt) -> $310.3 at Oct-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.83 x FY28 EPS $23.94. Q3 FCF conversion was 0.835 ($13,665M FCF / $16,372M non-GAAP net income) [1]; I round down because receivables and rack-related working capital grow with the ramp.
House base customer AI capex grows +22% in 2028 [14] and has no 2029 view; management only gives line of sight through FY28 [5]. Growth fades below the 2028 capex rate.
Below the 10-year Treasury yield of 5.31% [13]; nominal GDP-like.
10-year Treasury 5.31% on 2026-10-05 [13] + 5.5pt equity risk premium for a concentrated, 47%-realized-vol name (vol from the brief).

FY28 FCF discounted one year; terminal value (~50% of total) at end of FY37. Result $310.3/share. Net debt (debt $59,419M - cash $23,975M = $35.4B, ~$7/share [1]) is already reflected in FCF after interest.

bear.story: 2028 turns into a digestion year: the house low case has 2028 customer AI capex at $1,265B, below 2027's $1,390B [14]. Google shifts TPU volume to other sources (Q2 'diversity of sources' [6]; Macquarie models AVGO's share at 65% in 2028 [7]) and lab GW deployments slip. FY28 AI is flat at ~$115B, revenue $169B (non-AI $18B, software $36B), op margin 60% with less scale: EPS (169 x 0.60 - 2.4) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $16.83; at 15x (bottom of the peer range, NVDA 15.3x [12]) = $252. The contingent backstop ($29B max undiscounted, ~$5.9/share before rack resale value [3]) is a further tail, not included.

base.story: FY27 AI lands near the supply-secured ~$115B [5]; FY28 reaches ~$175B rather than $230B as Google splits supply and deployments lag, consistent with the 10-Q FY28 purchase commitments ($72,952M [4]) on FY27's commitments-to-revenue ratio. GM slides toward ~68-69% on XPU/rack mix; operating margin ~62%. EPS $23.94 x 18x = $431, blended 70/30 with a $310 DCF = ~$395.

bull.story: Management delivers FY28 AI of $230B [5], with Anthropic as the largest XPU customer in 2027 and Google 'multi-tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually' [5]; this needs roughly the house high capex path ($3,160B in 2028 [14]). Revenue $286B, op margin 63%: EPS (286 x 0.63 - 2.4) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $30.23 x 21x (inside the peer range, below the 23.7x median [12]) = $635.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount, argued from verified items that persist through Oct-2027: (1) Growth at the horizon: my FY28 EPS growth is +23% ($23.94 vs $19.39 [11]) against a peer median 'EPS next Y' of ~50% [12]; even management's >$30 FY28 EPS [5] is +55%, and the market already prices the largest, fastest-maturing AI-silicon names at the low end (NVDA 15.3x, TSM 21.8x, CSCO 20.8x [12]). (2) Concentration: 'only 6 customers', '4 of them are just simply going to be huge', and Anthropic 'on track to become our largest XPU customer in 2027' [5]. (3) Broadcom is underwriting customer financing: a $29B maximum undiscounted backstop over a 5-year lease term and a $42B uncommitted convertible-note facility ($0 drawn) to the customer [3]; management had nothing to announce on further residual value guarantees or backstops [5], and BofA moved Broadcom's issuer and bond ratings to Marketweight on XPV uncertainty [8]. (4) Mix-driven gross-margin dilution: 77.1% (Q2) -> 75.0% (Q3) -> ~73% (Q4 guide) [6][1][5]. Sell-side outperformance calls are not used. Peer set changes vs round 1: ARM (IP royalty, 99.5x) and MU (peak-cycle memory, 5.1x) dropped; CSCO and COHR added; basis switched from StockAnalysis mixed NTM to next-fiscal-year.

thesis_break_reason: ~13.9x FY27 consensus EPS ($19.39 [11]) and ~7% below the 52-week low of $289.96 (brief), a level set before the $115B/$230B AI targets existed. Trading there would most likely mean the market no longer believes the supply-secured ~$115B FY27 AI revenue [5]: a cut at the 2026-12-09 or March print, a lab customer deferring GW deployments, visible TPU share loss at Google beyond 'some diversity of sources' [6], a lease default that triggers the up-to-$29B backstop or a draw on the $42B note facility [3], or a 2027-28 capex cut toward the house low case [14]. It sits just above my bear-scenario value ($252), so a print there is closer to a broken thesis than to 47%-vol noise from a ~$395 centre.

reasoning: Round 2. What changed: the supervisor showed that two figures in my round-1 multiple and bear reasoning ($161.2B of Anthropic commitments; BofA's $370B peak RVG) were not verified at a primary source, that my Tan quote came from a BigGo recap, that my peer median mixed fiscal windows, and that my 40% FY27-stall leg was too heavy. I re-opened the primary documents. Verified at source: Q3 FY26 revenue $29,591M, AI $16.7B, non-GAAP op income $20,095M, non-GAAP NI $16,372M, EPS $3.32 on 4,937M shares, FCF $13,665M, non-GAAP interest $703M, debt $59,419M, cash $23,975M, Q4 guide $34.8B / AI $21.7B / op margin ~66% [1]; 10-Q R54: $29,000M max undiscounted backstop (5-yr), $42,000M uncommitted convertible-note facility, $0 drawn [3]; R53: purchase commitments $52,674M FY27, $72,952M FY28 [4]; call: $115B FY27 supply secured, $230B FY28 line of sight, FY28 EPS 'exceed $30', 16% tax, GM ~73%, 4.94B shares, report date 2026-12-09, 6 XPU customers / 4 huge, Anthropic largest in 2027, Anthropic 5 GW (2027) + 10 GW (2028), OpenAI 1.3 GW / >5 GW [5]; Q2 call: 'some diversity of sources' and GM 77.1% [6]; Macquarie 95/80/65% Google share and -21% FY28 EPS (sell-side estimates) [7]; FY27 consensus $19.39 [11]; Finviz peer P/Es [12]; 10y 5.31% [13]; house capex [14]. BofA's $370B is correctly quoted in the Investing.com article [8], but it is a sell-side model of a 20 GW build-out, not a disclosed exposure, so it stays out of every number (I agree with the supervisor here). Moody's and S&P comments on contingent obligations come only via a Deep News recap [9]: context, not in numbers. Removed from all numbers and text: $161.2B, $60B/$100B financing, SemiAnalysis/BigGo, Forkast/Finimize, Trefis segment margin, MarketBeat insider-sale figure. Valuation: rebuilt FY28 bottom-up: AI $175B, revenue $231B, op margin 62% (GM extrapolated from the Q2-Q4 mix trend), EPS $23.94; the same build at $230B gives $29.7, matching management's >$30, so the model is calibrated. The 10-Q commitments give an independent check: FY28 commitments are +38% on FY27, and on FY27's commitments/revenue ratio they imply ~$231B FY28 revenue, i.e. ~$175B AI, not $230B. Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep $175B (not $180B), because Google share erosion is on the record from the company itself [6], and the commitments cross-check lands at $175B. I keep 18x (not 19x), because horizon growth is half the peer median. My DCF uses 10.8% (not 10.5%) and a faster post-FY28 fade, so it comes out at $310 (supervisor $338). I replaced the stall leg with that DCF and moved the stall into the bear scenario. Fair value: 0.7 x 431.0 + 0.3 x 310.3 = $394.8. Scenarios 252/395/635 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$419). The ladder mixes three lognormals (sigma 0.32/0.28/0.30) around them: median $397.5 (reconciles with FV $394.8), mean ~$439, log-sd 0.44 (vs 47% realized), P(>=377) 0.549, P(<270) ~0.19. Base rates: a 47%-vol stock's one-year 1-sigma band is roughly $246-$632 around a $395 centre (395 x e^-0.47 to 395 x e^0.47), which the ladder spans. Sell-side targets are not used. Research limits: SEC refused a scripted fetch with a generic User-Agent, so filings were read with WebFetch; transcripts via Motley Fool.
